answer_1.quote: Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) have demonstrated significant capabilities across a spectrum of audio understanding and in-context learning tasks. These include instruction following, emotion recognition (ER), gender recognition (GR), speech question answering (SQA), and audio question answering (AQA).
answer_1.outputs: The generated outputs include responses to audio and text prompts in tasks such as audio question answering, emotion judgment, and context-based reasoning, where models generate natural language answers based on multimodal input.

answer_2.quote: Robustness is quantitatively assessed through three metrics: Defense Success Rate (DSR), Context Robustness Score (CRS), and Judgment Robustness Index (JRI).

answer_3.quote: This work uses a hybrid approach to evaluate model robustness, combining human assessment with an LLM-as-Judge method. Each of these 100 pairs was first judged by an LLM, then independently assessed by two human volunteers.

answer_4.quote: Each of these 100 pairs was first judged by an LLM, then independently assessed by two human volunteers.
answer_4.guideline: The human volunteers rated the model outputs according to predetermined criteria designed for a particular scenario (shown in the appendix), with a score range s of [0, 1]. The composite score s combines harmlessness (s_h) and consistency (s_c) through a weighted summation.
